items.commandOrSyntax: SELECT DISTINCT col1, col2 FROM table_name;
items.explanation: Retrieve unique deduplicated values across specified columns

items.explanation: Return the first non-NULL expression from left to right

items.commandOrSyntax: SELECT dept, COUNT(*), AVG(salary) FROM emp GROUP BY dept HAVING AVG(salary) > 50000;
items.explanation: Group rows and filter aggregated metrics using HAVING (WHERE cannot filter aggregates)

items.explanation: Count unique occurrences rather than total records
items.example: SELECT region, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_buyers FROM orders GROUP BY region;

items.commandOrSyntax: FROM table_a a INNER JOIN table_b b ON a.id = b.a_id
items.explanation: Returns records having matching keys in both tables
items.example: SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_name FROM orders o INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id;

items.commandOrSyntax: FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.id IS NULL;
items.explanation: Anti-join pattern: Identify customers who have never placed an order
items.example: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.cust_id WHERE o.cust_id IS NULL;

items.commandOrSyntax: ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY category ORDER BY sales DESC)
items.explanation: Assign sequential unique rank 1..N within each partitioned subset
items.example: SELECT product, category, sales, ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY category ORDER BY sales DESC) as rank_in_cat FROM products;

items.explanation: Access metric from previous row to compute period-over-period growth

items.explanation: Clean alternative to deeply nested IF statements; evaluates conditions sequentially
Returns the value when only one distinct value is selected in a slicer; otherwise returns default
Activates an inactive relationship inside a CALCULATE statement without changing the physical model
items.example: Sales by Ship Date = CALCULATE([Total Sales], USERELATIONSHIP(Orders[ShipDate], DimDate[Date]))

items.explanation: Always model relationships from 1-side (Dimension: Customers/Products) to Many-side (Fact: Orders/Sales) with Single cross-filter direction
Bi-directional filters cause ambiguity, performance degradation, and unexpected measure propagation in large enterprise models

title: Modern React & Component Architecture Master Cheatsheet
description: The definitive modern React engineering cheatsheet: component lifecycle, essential hooks (useState, useEffect), memoization (useMemo, useCallback), mutable refs, useReducer patterns, Context API, custom hooks patterns, and production performance tuning.

items.commandOrSyntax: export default function Component({ propA, propB = defaultValue }: Props)

{name}

{role}
; }

items.commandOrSyntax: List Rendering with Stable Key: items.map((item) => <Item key={item.id} {...item} />)
items.explanation: Always provide unique, stable IDs as keys—never array indices when lists can be reordered or filtered
Declares reactive state variable. Use updater function setState(prev => prev + 1) for concurrent/atomic updates
Synchronizes component with external systems (APIs, DOM listeners, timers). Always clean up subscriptions in return callback
items.example: useEffect(() => { const timer = setInterval(tick, 1000); return () => clearInterval(timer); }, []);

items.explanation: Holds a mutable value across renders without triggering a re-render. Commonly used for direct DOM access or interval IDs

items.commandOrSyntax: const memoizedValue = useMemo(() => computeHeavyData(a, b), [a, b])
items.explanation: Caches the result of an expensive calculation between renders unless dependencies change
items.example: const filteredUsers = useMemo(() => users.filter(u => u.role === selectedRole), [users, selectedRole]);

items.explanation: Preserves referential equality of a function instance to prevent unnecessary re-renders in memoized child components
items.example: const handleDelete = useCallback((id: string) => { setList(prev => prev.filter(x => x.id !== id)); }, []);

items.explanation: Higher-order component that skips re-rendering if props have not changed shallowly
items.example:
export const ProductRow = React.memo(function ProductRow({ item }: Props) { return
{item.title}
; });

sections.categoryTitle: 4. Complex State & Global State: useReducer & Context API

items.explanation: Manages complex state logic with explicit action types ({ type, payload }) following unidirectional Redux pattern
items.example: function reducer(state, action) { switch(action.type) { case 'ADD': return {...state, items: [...state.items, action.payload]}; default: return state; } }

items.explanation: Creates Context for prop-drilling prevention. Pair with ThemeContext.Provider and custom useContext consumer hook
items.example: export function useTheme() { const ctx = useContext(ThemeContext); if(!ctx) throw new Error('Outside Provider'); return ctx; }

items.explanation: Extracts reusable, testable stateful logic into pure JavaScript functions prefixed with 'use'
items.example: function useFetch<T>(url: string) { const [data, setData] = useState<T|null>(null); useEffect(() => { fetch(url).then(r => r.json()).then(setData); }, [url]); return { data }; }

items.explanation: Essential utility custom hooks for responsive UI listeners and search input rate limiting

items.commandOrSyntax: Single Source of Truth & Lifting State Up
items.explanation: Keep state at the lowest common ancestor that needs it. Avoid duplicating derived state that can be computed on the fly
items.example: Do not store 'fullName' in state if 'firstName' and 'lastName' are already in state; compute: const fullName = `${firstName} ${lastName}`

items.commandOrSyntax: Server Components vs Client Components ('use client')
items.explanation: In Next.js / modern React, components are Server Components by default (zero JS bundle). Add 'use client' only for hooks/events

title: Django & Django REST Framework (DRF) API Architecture Cheatsheet

items.explanation: Field-level and object-level validators. Raise serializers.ValidationError for bad input payloads
items.example: def validate_price(self, value): if value <= 0: raise serializers.ValidationError('Price must be positive'); return value

items.explanation: Guards endpoints against unauthorized HTTP operations
items.example: class IsOwnerOrReadOnly(permissions.BasePermission): def has_object_permission(self, req, view, obj): return req.method in permissions.SAFE_METHODS or obj.owner == req.user
